html:
The great assembly that, tradition says, met at Kouroukan Fouga near Kangaba after the Battle of Kirina, where Sundiata Keita and the Mande clans set the rules of the new Mali Empire.

It is said to have fixed the roles of the clans and castes, the rights of each group, rules of kinship joking between families that still ease conflicts, and protection for women and strangers. The text known today was assembled from oral traditions in the 20th century, so its details are debated. UNESCO listed the Manden Charter as intangible heritage in 2009. See also the Epic of Sundiata.
